newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, deferreds firm late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, deferreds firm late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower on softer world wheat prices, although deferred contracts firmed late on commercial buying, traders said.

U.S. wheat markets weakened early after Argentine wheat prices ebbed as sunny weather dried out soaked crops and allowed harvesting to progress. KCBT wheat also saw pressure from weakness in cash basis levels, which eased amid a slight increase in country movement, traders said.
KCBT wheat closed one to 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 3-3/4 cents at $4.08.
May lost 4-3/4 cents to close at $3.74-3/4.

"May took it on the chin today, but the sellers were mainly locals. You have to remember that all this was done on a lack of conviction. Volumes were very light," a KCBT trader said. "There just wasn't much news to trade today."
Traders said CIS bought 900,000 March bushels. Shay Grain and Wolcott Lincoln each sold 400,000 March.
